_about: The exam room's interface text (GAD-T544): ExamRoom, VoiceRoom, StaffNoticeBanner, WebcamIntegrity, ExaminerGaze, PracticeGaze and ExamRoomText (keys examRoom.<area>.<name>, read with UiText.For(the attempt's language)), and the text voice-room.js and examiner-gaze.js write (keys examRoom.js.<name>, rendered with <UiTextData Prefix="examRoom.js." /> and read with t() from js/ui-text.js, {name} slots). Razor text uses {0} slots (string.Format). Merged into en.json at startup; a key here may not repeat one there. docs/LOCALIZATION.md maps the keys.

examRoom.integrity.notice.strict: Integrity notes are on for this exam: if you switch to another tab or window, copy the question, leave full screen or have more than one screen connected, the browser notes when and for how long, for your instructor to review. They are notes, never an automatic fail, and nothing is blocked. Your browser may ask to allow screen detection; you can decline.

They are notes, never an automatic fail, and nothing is blocked. Your browser may ask to allow screen detection; you can decline.

examRoom.gaze.noteAccommodated: You have an eye-contact accommodation: you don't need to look at the examiner, and the examiner won't remind you to. Your camera still checks, on your device only, that your face is in view and that you are on your own; if not, the examiner will say so. A short note of when it happened is kept for a person to review.
examRoom.gaze.note: Your camera checks, on your device only, where you look while you answer. Looking away to think is normal and fine: nothing happens while you work out your answer before you start speaking, and glancing at anything on the screen (the transcript, the clock) never counts. Only a long look off the screen while you speak does: then the examiner gives a small nod of the head, the screen around her may dim a little (it clears as soon as you look back), and at a pause she may say a short, friendly line. "Set up eye contact again" has you follow a dot for about 10 seconds so the camera learns your screen, which makes the check fairer. A short note of a long look away is kept for a person to review; it is never a grade and never decides anything. If you can't keep eye contact (for example for a disability), ask your instructor for the eye-contact accommodation.
examRoom.gaze.notePractice: Your camera checks, on your device only, where you look while you answer, exactly as in an exam. Looking away to think is normal and fine: nothing happens while you work out your answer, and glancing at anything on the screen never counts. Only a long look off the screen while you speak does: the examiner gives a small nod, the screen around her may dim a little (it clears as soon as you look back), and at a pause she may say a short, friendly line. "Set up eye contact again" has you follow a dot for about 10 seconds so the camera learns your screen. In an exam a short note of a long look away is kept for a person to review; in this practice nothing is kept.

examRoom.js.avatar.none: The examiner's picture could not start; questions are read out by your browser and shown as text.

examRoom.js.gaze.setup: Follow the dot with your eyes and keep your head still. It takes about 10 seconds.
examRoom.js.gaze.on: Eye contact check on. Looking away to think is fine.
examRoom.js.gaze.noFace: Your face isn't in view of the camera.

examRoom.js.gaze.accommodated: Eye contact isn't required for you (accommodation). The camera only checks that your face is in view.
examRoom.js.gaze.unavailable: Eye contact isn't being checked: the camera check couldn't start on this device. The exam carries on.
examRoom.js.gaze.setupCaption: Follow the dot with your eyes and keep your head still. Esc or Skip stops.
examRoom.js.gaze.setupRetry: Not quite precise enough. Once more: sit still and look right at the centre of each dot.
